helter skelter.title: Helter skelter
helter skelter.author: Vincent Bugliosi and Curt Gentry
helter skelter.why: The prosecutor's account of the Manson murders and trial; a gripping true-crime classic.

brief wondrous life of oscar wao.title: The Brief Wondrous Life of Oscar Wao
brief wondrous life of oscar wao.author: Junot Diaz
brief wondrous life of oscar wao.why: A nerdy Dominican-American boy and his family under a curse and a dictator; brilliant, voice-driven and slang-rich.

godkiller.title: Godkiller
godkiller.author: Hannah Kaner
godkiller.why: A hunter of dangerous gods teams up with a girl and a child in a high fantasy world; readers had a book hangover.

running with scissors.title: Running with Scissors
running with scissors.author: Augusten Burroughs
running with scissors.why: Burroughs' darkly comic memoir of a bizarre childhood with his mother's psychiatrist's family.

wise mans fear.title: The Wise Man's Fear
wise mans fear.author: Patrick Rothfuss
wise mans fear.why: Second book of the Kingkiller Chronicle; Kvothe's tale continues, though fans wait years for the finale.

plot against america.title: The Plot Against America
plot against america.author: Philip Roth
plot against america.why: Comments are mixed and mostly describe it as boring.

scar tissue.title: Scar Tissue
scar tissue.author: Anthony Kiedis and Larry Sloman
scar tissue.why: The Red Hot Chili Peppers singer's brutally honest memoir of addiction and survival; strong on audio.

tai pan.title: Tai-Pan
tai pan.author: James Clavell
tai pan.why: Clavell's sweeping tale of rival traders founding Hong Kong; a long, gripping adventure.

exorcist.title: The Exorcist
exorcist.author: William Peter Blatty
exorcist.why: A girl's possession and the priests who fight it; readers call it superbly written and genuinely scary.

behind the beautiful forevers.title: Behind the Beautiful Forevers
behind the beautiful forevers.author: Katherine Boo
behind the beautiful forevers.why: Reported story of families in a Mumbai slum; gorgeous writing that left readers traumatized.

still life with woodpecker.title: Still Life with Woodpecker
still life with woodpecker.author: Tom Robbins
still life with woodpecker.why: Tom Robbins' wacky love story of an outlaw princess and a bomber; readers burst out laughing.

summer sisters.title: Summer sisters
summer sisters.author: Judy Blume
summer sisters.why: Two women's friendship from childhood to middle age in Judy Blume's adult novel.

dont let the forest in.title: Don't Let the Forest In
dont let the forest in.author: C. G. Drews
dont let the forest in.why: Two teens face a dark fairy-tale forest; a gothic, atmospheric YA horror favourite.

mansfield park.title: Mansfield Park
mansfield park.author: Jane Austen
mansfield park.why: Austen's quieter novel of a poor cousin raised in a rich house; divisive heroine but rewarding.

pilgrim at tinker creek.title: Pilgrim at Tinker Creek
pilgrim at tinker creek.author: Annie Dillard
pilgrim at tinker creek.why: Dillard's observations of nature near her Virginia home; gorgeous, meditative writing that earned a Pulitzer.

book of the unnamed midwife.title: The Book of the Unnamed Midwife
book of the unnamed midwife.author: Meg Elison
book of the unnamed midwife.why: A midwife survives a plague that kills most women in a bleak post-apocalypse; readers reread it often.

maybe you should talk to someone.title: Maybe You Should Talk to Someone
maybe you should talk to someone.author: Lori Gottlieb
maybe you should talk to someone.why: A therapist goes to therapy herself; readers find it funny, warm and keeps making them laugh.

something happened.title: Something Happened
something happened.author: Joseph Heller
something happened.why: An anxious executive's inner monologue from the author of Catch-22; divisive, sad and eye-opening.

edible woman.title: The Edible Woman
edible woman.author: Margaret Atwood
edible woman.why: Comments do not clearly recommend this book.

glass bead game.title: The Glass Bead Game
glass bead game.author: Hermann Hesse
glass bead game.why: A scholar rises in an intellectual order devoted to a game of ideas; demanding, richly philosophical.

stormlight archives.title: The Stormlight Archive
stormlight archives.author: Brandon Sanderson
stormlight archives.why: Sanderson's ongoing epic series of huge books, praised for original worldbuilding and magic.

warlock.title: Warlock
warlock.author: Oakley Hall
warlock.why: A Western about a town and its gunman showing how perspectives change over time.

born to run.title: Born to Run
born to run.author: Bruce Springsteen
born to run.why: Springsteen's memoir in literary prose; especially good as an audiobook he narrates himself.

on the calculation of volume.title: On the Calculation of Volume
on the calculation of volume.author: Solvej Balle
on the calculation of volume.why: A woman is stuck repeating the same day in this quiet, much-praised Danish series.

heart shaped box.title: Heart-Shaped Box
heart shaped box.author: Joe Hill
heart shaped box.why: An aging rock star buys a ghost online; readers say it scared them badly.

thorn birds.title: The Thorn Birds
thorn birds.author: Colleen McCullough
thorn birds.why: Epic Australian family saga of love and a forbidden priest; readers call it a piece of art.

hero and the crown.title: The Hero and the Crown
hero and the crown.author: Robin McKinley
hero and the crown.why: A girl becomes a dragon-slaying hero in a classic fantasy that turned many young readers into book lovers.

mother mary comes to me.title: Mother Mary Comes to Me
mother mary comes to me.author: Arundhati Roy
mother mary comes to me.why: Roy's memoir about her mother and her own path; readers who liked The God of Small Things find it incredible.

boys in the boat.title: The Boys in the Boat
boys in the boat.author: Daniel James Brown
boys in the boat.why: Story of the 1936 US Olympic rowing team told with narrative drive; a popular inspirational read.

end of eternity.title: The End of Eternity
end of eternity.author: Isaac Asimov
end of eternity.why: A time-travel novel with paradoxes galore; some readers call it Asimov's best.

interior chinatown.title: Interior Chinatown
interior chinatown.author: Charles Yu
interior chinatown.why: A background actor dreams of being the lead in the script of a cop show; formatted as a screenplay and sharply funny.

weaveworld.title: Weaveworld
weaveworld.author: Clive Barker
weaveworld.why: A hidden magical world woven into a carpet is hunted; readers find it mind-bending dark fantasy.

bill the galactic hero.title: Bill the Galactic Hero
bill the galactic hero.author: Harry Harrison
bill the galactic hero.why: A farm boy is drafted into an absurd space war in this antiwar parody of military sf.

straight man.title: Straight Man
straight man.author: Richard Russo
straight man.why: A reluctant college English department head faces a crisis in this campus comedy; readers say it is the funniest book they've read.

peripheral.title: The Peripheral
peripheral.author: William Gibson
peripheral.why: Gibson's story of a woman who finds a link to a future London; fantastic but telegraphic and demanding.

other valley.title: The other Valley
other valley.author: Scott Alexander Howard
other valley.why: A town sealed between a valley of the past and the future; readers call it the best they've read.

favorites.title: The Favorites
favorites.author: Layne Fargo
favorites.why: Olympic figure skating partners fall into love and scandal, told like a documentary; compelling and dramatic.

pale king.title: The Pale King
pale king.author: David Foster Wallace
pale king.why: Unfinished novel about boredom at an IRS center; hard and frustrating, but admired by DFW fans.

ring.title: Ring
ring.author: Stephen Baxter
ring.why: Hard sci-fi in the Xeelee universe with huge ideas and immense time spans.

heart is a lonely hunter.title: The Heart is a Lonely Hunter
heart is a lonely hunter.author: Carson McCullers
heart is a lonely hunter.why: Lonely misfits in a Southern town gather around a deaf man; a moving American classic.

right stuff.title: The Right Stuff
right stuff.author: Tom Wolfe
right stuff.why: Wolfe's vivid account of the Mercury astronauts and test pilots; an all-time great of narrative non-fiction.

blackwater.title: Blackwater
blackwater.author: Michael McDowell
blackwater.why: A six-part Southern gothic saga of a river family and its mysterious matriarch; fantastic and bingeable.

future.title: The Future
future.author: Naomi Alderman
future.why: Alderman imagines tech billionaires and the end of the world; readers are sucked in and want to reread it.

book of form and emptiness.title: The Book of Form and Emptiness
book of form and emptiness.author: Ruth L. Ozeki
book of form and emptiness.why: A boy hears objects speak after his father dies, and finds help in a library; tender and imaginative.

girl interrupted.title: Girl, Interrupted
girl interrupted.author: Susanna Kaysen
girl interrupted.why: Kaysen's short memoir of her time in a psychiatric hospital in the 1960s.

elena knows.title: Elena Knows
elena knows.author: Claudia Piñeiro
elena knows.why: A sick mother searches for who killed her daughter; the ending reveals how good it is.

cosmicomics.title: Cosmicomics
cosmicomics.author: Italo Calvino
cosmicomics.why: Playful surreal stories narrated by a shape-shifting being across cosmic history; lovely and inventive.

cry the beloved country.title: Cry, the Beloved Country
cry the beloved country.author: Alan Paton
cry the beloved country.why: A Zulu pastor searches for his son in Johannesburg during apartheid; moving and lyrical.

only forward.title: Only forward
only forward.author: Michael Marshall Smith
only forward.why: A noir detective romp in a strange future city that turns deeper; readers beg others to find it.

book of longings.title: The Book of Longings
book of longings.author: Sue Monk Kidd
book of longings.why: Imagined life of Jesus' wife, an independent woman in ancient Galilee; readers like its feminist take.

transcendent kingdom.title: Transcendent Kingdom
transcendent kingdom.author: Yaa Gyasi
transcendent kingdom.why: A neuroscientist reckons with family addiction and faith; readers were in shambles afterwards.

last one.title: The Last One
last one.author: Will Dean
last one.why: A fast, twist-filled thriller; readers call it bonkers and addictive, though some found it too long.

witch.title: The Witch
witch.author: Marie NDiaye
witch.why: Comments do not discuss this book.

death in her hands.title: Death in Her Hands
death in her hands.author: Ottessa Moshfegh
death in her hands.why: An old woman finds a note about a murdered girl and her imagination takes over; unsettling Moshfegh.

american tragedy.title: An American Tragedy
american tragedy.author: Theodore Dreiser
american tragedy.why: A poor young man's ambition leads to murder and trial; long but easy to follow.

sword of shannara.title: The Sword of Shannara
sword of shannara.author: Terry Brooks
sword of shannara.why: Classic quest fantasy that got many readers started on the genre.

cipher.title: The Cipher
cipher.author: Kathe Koja
cipher.why: A video store clerk is drawn to a strange hole in the floor in this bleak cult horror.

midnight in chernobyl.title: Midnight in Chernobyl
midnight in chernobyl.author: Adam Higginbotham
midnight in chernobyl.why: The extraordinarily well-told story of the Chernobyl disaster and its causes.

watchers.title: Watchers
watchers.author: Dean Koontz
watchers.why: Comments are mixed, with one calling it cheesy.

stella maris.title: Stella Maris
stella maris.author: Cormac McCarthy
stella maris.why: A mathematician speaks with her psychiatrist in dialogue form; brilliant, smart and dense.

mandy.title: Mandy
mandy.author: Julie Edwards
mandy.why: An orphan finds a hidden cottage to make her own; whimsical and wonderful.

sundial.title: The Sundial
sundial.author: Shirley Jackson
sundial.why: A family prepares for the end of the world in a big house; an extremely mean Shirley Jackson novel.

true confessions of charlotte doyle.title: The True Confessions of Charlotte Doyle
true confessions of charlotte doyle.author: Avi
true confessions of charlotte doyle.why: A girl sails on a ship with a mutinous crew; a children's favourite.

yumi and the nightmare painter.title: Yumi and the Nightmare Painter
yumi and the nightmare painter.author: Brandon Sanderson
yumi and the nightmare painter.why: A standalone Cosmere romance between a girl and an artist who paint in dreams; easy and captivating.

one dark window.title: One Dark Window
one dark window.author: Rachel Gillig
one dark window.why: Comments are split, including a clearly uninvested reader.

her smoke rose up forever.title: Her Smoke Rose Up Forever
her smoke rose up forever.author: James Tiptree, Jr.
her smoke rose up forever.why: Tiptree's collected stories, intense and moving; best taken in small doses.

scarlet letter.title: The Scarlet Letter
scarlet letter.author: Nathaniel Hawthorne
scarlet letter.why: A woman in Puritan Boston bears a mark of shame; a tough but rewarding school classic.

jack dawkins.title: Jack Dawkins
jack dawkins.author: Charlton Daines
jack dawkins.why: The Artful Dodger as an adult in a Dickens-flavoured adventure; familiar and fun.

liliths brood.title: Lilith's Brood
liliths brood.author: Octavia E. Butler
liliths brood.why: Aliens save humanity after nuclear war at a cost; a master class in human motivation.

big sleep.title: The Big Sleep
big sleep.author: Raymond Chandler
big sleep.why: Philip Marlowe takes a case among gangsters and corrupt cops; the classic hard-boiled mystery.
